growing_tip.body_text: Sucrine (Little gem mini Lettuce) | → Dragoon → Bambi → Winter Density → 4 rows (8”-20 cm) per bed spaced every 6” (15 cm) on the row → Sucrine will do great in beds that were previously amended with compost and fertilized with a mix of alfalfa meal (2-0-2) and pelleted chicken manure (5-3-2). | → Rotary harrow → 30” bed prep rake → Popping tray and marking roller → Remove tarp and clean out large debris. Use the rake if needed.* → Uniformly apply amendments and pass with the rotary harrow at a depth of 2” (5 cm). To make transplanting easier (seeing as the soil is loose after being harrowed), we only prepare the beds when we are about to transplant. → Pass with the dibbler-roller to mark the planting holes and bring out the well-watered trays. → Once the beds are ready, 1 person will drop the seedlings while 2 others transplant as fast as possible. Sucrine seedlings are very hardy and don’t need special care. 3 people/100’ bed is a good ratio for efficient workflow. → Install irrigation and water the soil until it is deeply moistened. * If the previous crop is too well established, or if the bed is too messy, mow the crop as low as possible and harrow at a depth of 2” (5 cm). Add 1’’ (2.5 cm) of compost evenly spread on the whole width of the bed and transplant into compost following a no-till strategy. → Sucrines are cultivated using the flex tine weeder 10 to 12 days after implantation when the weeds are at the filament/cotyledon stage. In weedy beds, a second pass should be planned 7 days later. → Slugs and aphids are sometimes present, but rarely enough to justify an intervention. 2 → Sucrines are harvested in the fields in a kneeling position. → Harvesting is done using a VERY sharp knife. Sharpen your blades before each harvest; this will help reduce potential oxidation (browning or discolouration) on the cut surface. irrigation.body_text: → Drip tape (4 per bed) or sprinkler | → Root depth: Shallow (6”-24”) → General: Water consistently for succulent growth and to avoid bitter taste. Sucrine is a good crop to grow for restaurants or other sales outlets where deliveries can be expected weekly over a long period of the year. They are somewhat frost tolerant, chic and generate great yields per square foot. We plant sucrine every 2 weeks to ensure a constant supply throughout our growing season. For every seeding, we plan enough beds for an estimated 2 weeks of harvest. In our planting program, sucrine is grouped with green onions, chicory, mini-fennel and head lettuce  —  all crops that stay in the fields +/- 50 days and that have similar crop requirements. 1
